copy.app.tagline: See your photo the way a stalker's AI would, before you post it.
copy.app.oneLiner: The cloud plays the attacker. Your device holds the answers. The attacker never learns whether it guessed right.
copy.welcome.b1: AI can work out where a photo was taken from the pixels alone, even with location data removed.
copy.welcome.b2: Strangers' Eyes lets a cloud AI attack a redacted copy, then grades it on this device against what you need to hide.
copy.welcome.b3: Your vault and your original photo never leave this device.
copy.welcome.age: I'm 18 or older, and I'll only check photos I took or own.

copy.about.howItWorks: Your private vault stays on this device and acts as the answer key. · An on-device referee grades the cloud attacker, which never sees the result. · An Egress Gate checks every request and blocks leaks before they happen. · What runs where is set by data sensitivity, and shown live.
copy.about.reattackDisclosure: When you re-attack, the cloud sees which areas you masked, but never why.
copy.about.support: If you're worried someone is tracking you, contact a local domestic-violence or victim-support service.

copy.judge.coach.prescreen: Faces and text are found on this device and checked against the fake vault before anything goes to the attacker. Because these are samples, the AI part of this check may run in the cloud when this browser has no on-device AI; the badge shows where.
copy.judge.coach.consent: This is the exact redacted copy the cloud attacker gets: faces and vault text are solid-masked and metadata is removed. In autoplay, samples send themselves after 3 s; your own photos never go without your tap.
copy.judge.coach.attack: Gemini in the cloud plays the stranger and studies only that redacted copy. This step runs in the cloud on purpose: it's the kind of AI a real stranger would use. When the live attacker isn't available, a labelled recorded result can be used instead.
copy.judge.coach.referee: The attacker's guesses are graded against the vault. With your real vault this only ever runs on this device, or as built-in rules; this vault is fake, so it may use the cloud.
copy.judge.coach.verdict: Distances to the vault's pins are worked out by code and shown as bands, never as a map pin or an address. The cloud never learns whether it was right.
copy.judge.coach.fix: The smallest fix (masks or a crop) is planned from the clues the attacker used. Like the referee, it stays on this device with your real vault; with this fake vault it may use the cloud.
copy.judge.coach.reattack: The fixed copy goes back to the cloud attacker to check whether the clues still work. The cloud sees which areas were masked, but never why.

ui.cap.howto.title: How to turn on on-device AI in Chrome
ui.cap.howto.step1: Open chrome://settings/ai and turn on On-device AI.
ui.cap.howto.step2: If your Chrome lists it, set chrome://flags/#prompt-api-for-gemini-nano-multimodal-input to Enabled.
ui.cap.howto.step3: Restart Chrome, then come back to this page.
ui.cap.howto.hardware: On-device AI needs at least 22 GB of free disk space and either a GPU with more than 4 GB of video memory or 16 GB of RAM (on a Mac, macOS 13 or later).

ui.about.leaves.S0: Never. It runs on this device with Gemini Nano, or as built-in rules.
ui.about.leaves.S1: Never. The first look for clues runs on this device.
ui.about.leaves.S2: Only when this device can't run it, or Gemini Nano is turned off, and never with your vault's words or places in it.
ui.about.leaves.S3: Yes: only the redacted copy you approve, with faces and vault text solid-masked and metadata removed.
ui.about.leaves.S4: May go to the cloud when this browser has no on-device AI, or Gemini Nano is turned off. Nothing in them is real.
ui.about.gemini: The cloud attacker is Gemini, reached through Firebase AI Logic, and it only ever gets the redacted copy you approve. Public explanations and Judge Mode samples also use Gemini when on-device AI isn't available or is turned off.
ui.about.recaptcha: App Check loads Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise to confirm that requests come from this app.
ui.about.lib.mediapipe: MediaPipe Tasks Vision and the BlazeFace models (face detection) · Apache-2.0
ui.about.lib.tesseract: Tesseract.js and the Tesseract OCR cores (text reading) · Apache-2.0
ui.about.licenses: Licence texts of the bundled code
ui.about.prior.e11: A location-awareness app powered by a large language model, studied with 19 participants over 2 weeks (ACM CHI 2025, arXiv 2503.20226).
ui.about.prior.e12: A TikTok TechJam 2025 project: Gemini 2.5 Flash finds the clues, Grounding DINO draws boxes and OpenCV blurs them, on a cloud GPU backend.
ui.about.prior.diff: Strangers' Eyes differs by grading the attacker on this device, against a private vault the cloud never sees.
ui.about.adults: Strangers' Eyes is for adults (18+). Only check photos you took or own.
